# Round 4, H1 to H4 (docs/gpu-experiments/04-kernels/04-router-merge-split.md). The router and the merge one
# level deeper are the pushed header, not a flag, so H1 and H3 read their exec from queue-f3.txt's G4 row
# (the router against 16 us, the merge against 13.7). Here: the router in four tasks (H2, --router-tasks)
# and the merge as regular tasks (H4, --merge-tasks, then two per head), each the pair on the 2-layer
# graph with the GEMV stack.
--layers 2 --iters 1 --tile-linears --nt-weights --event-timing --fuse-norm2 --fuse-silu --fuse-norm1 --mfma-attend --attend-tasks --nt-streams --gemv-linears --gemv-w13 --router-tasks compare continue    # H2: the ids and the route log equal
--layers 2 --iters 32 --tile-linears --nt-weights --event-timing --fuse-norm2 --fuse-silu --fuse-norm1 --mfma-attend --attend-tasks --nt-streams --gemv-linears --gemv-w13 --router-tasks table continue    # H2: the router gap against H1's
--layers 2 --iters 1 --tile-linears --nt-weights --event-timing --fuse-norm2 --fuse-silu --fuse-norm1 --mfma-attend --attend-tasks --nt-streams --gemv-linears --gemv-w13 --merge-tasks compare continue    # H4: one task per head
--layers 2 --iters 32 --tile-linears --nt-weights --event-timing --fuse-norm2 --fuse-silu --fuse-norm1 --mfma-attend --attend-tasks --nt-streams --gemv-linears --gemv-w13 --merge-tasks table continue    # H4
--layers 2 --iters 1 --tile-linears --nt-weights --event-timing --fuse-norm2 --fuse-silu --fuse-norm1 --mfma-attend --attend-tasks --nt-streams --gemv-linears --gemv-w13 --merge-tasks --merge-halves 2 compare continue    # H4: two tasks per head
--layers 2 --iters 32 --tile-linears --nt-weights --event-timing --fuse-norm2 --fuse-silu --fuse-norm1 --mfma-attend --attend-tasks --nt-streams --gemv-linears --gemv-w13 --merge-tasks --merge-halves 2 table continue    # H4
